eyebrow: CHARITY RESEARCH · SAN FRANCISCO · ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH
program: Street-tree planting, establishment care, sidewalk gardens, and workforce development

nutshell.headline: FUF's San Francisco tree delivery is verified, but its health effect per surviving street-tree-year is not.
nutshell.body: Under an explicitly judgmental signed prior-weighted illustration, a $100,000 unrestricted gift corresponds to $1.053 million per better life (10 modeled QALYs), or $1.219 million including a gross-resource sensitivity. The 10%-weight favorable case supplies 84.9% of expected net QALYs. These are not empirical marginal estimates; verified marginal donor and gross costs remain unknown.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: San Francisco Public Works verified grant-associated reporting of 1,412 trees planted in FY2023–24 and extended a large performance-based grant. FUF provides establishment care and directs gifts toward low-canopy San Francisco neighborhoods.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: No study identifies QALYs per surviving San Francisco street-tree-year, FUF publishes no matched survival, and the cited city contract has expired without a public current marginal gift plan.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Obtain current tree and survival cohorts, approved-site backlog, contract status, marginal gift allocation, and an independently defensible health-utility or morbidity bridge for comparable San Francisco blocks.

summary.label: MODELED ORDINARY GIFT
summary.detail: signed prior-weighted per 10 modeled QALYs; 84.9% favorable-tail driven

summary.label: CENTRAL ILLUSTRATION
summary.detail: per 10 modeled QALYs using an unvalidated 0.010 QALY/tree-year scalar

summary.label: FAVORABLE ILLUSTRATION

summary.detail: direct gift pathway and deficit, but prior city contract expired and no priced current tranche

programSection.body: FUF plants and establishes San Francisco street trees, installs sidewalk gardens, conducts outreach, and runs youth and workforce-development activities.

steps.title: Identify and prepare planting sites
steps.detail: FUF coordinates utilities, residents, species selection, concrete removal, and community planting in low-canopy neighborhoods.

steps.title: Plant and establish trees
steps.detail: San Francisco Public Works' grant-performance section reported 1,412 trees planted in FY2023–24; this may be a subset, not a full organization census. FUF's historical report describes three years of establishment care.

steps.title: Deliver broader community programs
steps.detail: Gardens, outreach, volunteers, youth, and workforce development remain in whole-organization cost but receive no separately stacked health credit.

programSection.boundary: The full FY2024 IRS expense of $5,673,426 is used. Dividing by 1,412 trees reported in the city grant-performance section gives $4,018 per credited grant-associated tree-output equivalent and 24.89 equivalents for a $100,000 expense share. The 1,412 may be a subset rather than a complete organization census, while all organization cost is charged. This is retrospective accounting scale, not a verified marginal tree purchase.

model.headline: Prior-weighted modeled ordinary gift: $1.053M per 10 QALYs; central: $1.848M.
model.body: The model converts only additional surviving, discounted tree-years through an explicit analyst health scalar. It does not add heat, pollution, mental health, physical activity, mortality, gardens, workforce, or climate benefits separately.

equation.label: CENTRAL MODELED GIFT COST
equation.expression: 10 × $100,000 ÷ [(9.955 incremental trees × 5.634 finite discounted surviving tree-years/tree × 0.010 QALY/tree-year) − (9.955 incremental trees × 0.002 harm QALY/tree)]
equation.result: $1,848,441 per 10 modeled QALYs; 0.540996 gift-attributed net QALY

inputs.label: Gift-linked credited tree-output equivalents
inputs.confidence: High arithmetic; moderate output matching; low census completeness and marginality
inputs.range: same retrospective base in all scenarios
inputs.basis: $100,000 / $5,673,426 × 1,412 trees from the city grant-performance section. This is verified grant-associated output, not proven complete whole-organization output; all organization cost is still charged. Watering, care visits, and gardens are not added as beneficiaries.

inputs.label: Scenario prior weights
inputs.basis: Delivery is verified, but health conversion, current additionality, and FUF survival are not; harm plus null therefore receive 60% weight.

inputs.label: Ordinary-gift funding additionality
inputs.basis: The donation page promises more trees and both FY2024 and FY2025 had deficits. The cited city contract expired and no current approved-site or gift tranche is public.

inputs.label: Establishment survival and annual post-establishment mortality
inputs.basis: FUF provides three years of establishment care. The review reports annual cohort-mortality quartiles around 2.8%–9.3%, highest in the first five years; scenarios apply explicit year-by-year decay. No FUF cohort survival is public.

inputs.label: Finite benefit horizon
inputs.basis: Tree-years are explicitly finite and discounted at 3%; no perpetual canopy benefit is credited.

inputs.label: QALY per surviving tree-year
inputs.basis: External studies support plausibility but do not identify this value. Central equals one aggregate QALY per 100 surviving tree-years; favorable equals four. Neither is an empirical FUF effect.

inputs.label: Harm QALY per incremental tree
inputs.basis: Represents allergens, impaired ventilation, water, root or sidewalk damage, failure risk, maintenance, and green-gentrification burdens; no FUF incidence is alleged.

inputs.label: Gross-resource multiplier
inputs.basis: Stresses volunteer and resident time plus downstream city care. Water, property-owner effort, and infrastructure costs remain unknown.

inputs.label: Bay and San Francisco direct-health shares
inputs.confidence: High for tree location; not unique beneficiaries
inputs.basis: Verified trees are planted in San Francisco; benefits may reach residents, workers, and visitors. Bay and SF are nested.

sensitivity.headline: −0.07466 modeled QALY
sensitivity.detail: No positive ratio; a signed burden stress, not observed FUF harm.

sensitivity.headline: No positive QALYs
sensitivity.detail: No validated tree-health conversion; donor and gross ratios are null.

sensitivity.headline: $1.848M modeled donor cost per 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 0.540996 net gift QALY and $2.218M modeled gross-resource cost.

sensitivity.headline: $124,101 modeled donor cost per 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 8.05794 net gift QALYs and $186,152 modeled gross-resource cost.

sensitivity.headline: $1.053M modeled donor cost per 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 0.949427 expected net QALY and $1.219M modeled gross-resource cost. The favorable case contributes 84.9% of expected net QALYs; without it, donor cost is $6.27M.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Scenario weights and all health-conversion values are analyst priors, not confidence intervals or measured FUF effects. The weighted result is favorable-tail-sensitive. A zero-funding sensitivity returns zero QALYs and null donor, gross, Bay, and SF ratios or shares.
model.fundingBoundary: RFMF is a moderate physical pathway with unverified current gift additionality. FUF says donations support more trees in low-canopy San Francisco neighborhoods. The newer FY2025 filing reports $5.142M revenue, $5.410M expense, a $268K deficit, and $2.327M net assets. But the cited $5.551M city contract ended 2025-08-31, and no current approved-site backlog, renewal, binding match, survival target, or next-$100,000 allocation is public. Verified marginal donor and gross costs are null.

evidence.design: San Francisco Public Works grant-performance memo
evidence.population: Grant-associated FUF FY2023–24 San Francisco delivery
evidence.result: The grant-performance section reports 1,412 trees planted, 1,172 watered weekly, 2,909 care visits, and 2,364 square feet of gardens; performance supported a contract extension through August 2025.
evidence.transfer: Strong delivery verification but not proof of a complete whole-organization tree census. The reported trees form a conservative credited denominator while all cost is charged; other activities are not added as health beneficiaries, and the expired contract is not current funding room.

evidence.population: Adults living near treated vacant lots in Philadelphia
evidence.result: Depression and worthlessness were lower near greened lots, but the package combined grass, trees, fencing, and maintenance; overall poor mental health was not significantly reduced.
evidence.transfer: Supports mechanism plausibility but does not isolate a street-tree effect or QALYs.

evidence.result: Project reporting describes reduced inflammatory biomarkers after large-scale planting.
evidence.transfer: An intermediate endpoint only; receives zero clinical-event or mortality QALYs.

evidence.population: Portland neighborhoods with nonprofit tree planting
evidence.result: More and older planted trees were associated with lower later mortality.
evidence.transfer: Residual confounding and city/intervention transfer prevent direct causal conversion.

evidence.population: Whole FUF legal organization, FY ending June 2024
evidence.result: Expense $5.673M, revenue $5.007M, deficit $666K, net assets $2.595M, and contributions $4.971M.
evidence.transfer: Full expense remains in the donor denominator; financial need does not prove marginal tree output.

reservations: No source supplies QALYs per surviving San Francisco street-tree-year.
FUF publishes no matched survival by cohort, species, or neighborhood.
The $2,500 price is historical FY2021–22, not a current restricted offer.
The 1,412 trees are verified grant-associated output, not proven complete whole-organization output; all organization expense is nevertheless charged.
The FY2023–24 output/expense ratio does not prove marginal constant returns.
External greening evidence differs in intervention, setting, outcome, and causal strength.
Scenario weights, additionality, survival, horizon, health scalar, harm, and gross multipliers are priors.
Current public-funding substitution and downstream city/resource costs are incomplete.
excludedBenefits: Separately stacked heat, pollution, noise, asthma, physical-activity, mental-health, and mortality pathways
